An article on Ghost Sharks by Gareth Fraser published in Australian Geographic
An article “Chasing Ghosts” by Associate Professor Gareth Fraser about his work on the Australian Ghost Shark was published in Australian Geographic. Article Here
Read More
Yao Lab publishes papers in iScience and Nature.
The Yao Lab has recently published a paper in iScience. This work was carried out by former technicians Dimitrios Giakoumas and Julia Zhu, high-school student Alaina Jamal, and Assistant Professor Zepeng Yao. In this study, the authors systematically identified pharyngeal and gut sensory axons in the Drosophila brain connectome and mapped their downstream circuits. […]
Read More
Associate Professor Keith Choe awarded NSF grant
Ketih Choe and collaborator Gail Fanucci (UF Chem) have been awarded an NSF grant to study metal-responsive biomolecular condensates in C. elegans. Congratulations Keith! Title: Understanding the role of C. elegans histidine-rich protein condensates in metal homeostasis This project combines expertise of a C. elegans stress physiology lab and a protein chemistry lab […]
Read More
New horizontal gene transfer discovery in rare plants by Dr. Liming Cai
New horizontal gene transfer discovery in rare plants by Dr. Liming Cai Assistant professor Liming Cai has discovered the first known HGT (horizontal gene transfer) interaction between a rare New Caledonian plant and a parasitic plant using the tool HGTscanner. Liming’s study was published in Methods in Ecology and Evolution. […]
Read More
Book published by Jack Putz (under the pseudonym Juan Camilo Moro): Gone Science on the Rio Negro.
Gone Science Jack Putz’s most recent foray into fiction, again writing as Juan Camilo Moro, tracks two graduate students as they join an international research project in Amazonian Venezuela. Gone Science on the Rio Negro will delight aficionados of the jungle fiction genre with its irreverent portrayals of prominent scientists along with lots of […]
